summary: Yoshinori Takeuchi (1913–2002) was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Hajime Tanabe at Kyoto University (~1933–1946), where he later served as associate professor (1948) and professor (1959–1976), followed by Aichi Gakuin University (~1977–1988).

Yoshio Kawakatsu (1922–1984) worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1945–1948) and under Paul Demiéville (~1958–1960). From around 1952 to 1984, he served as a library assistant at Kyoto University.
Yoshio Nishiguchi is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida.
Yoshio Takeuchi (1886–1966) was a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (~1907–1910) and held a post at Tohoku University from around 1923 to 1946.

Yoshiro Imaeda (born 1947) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Otani University, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University under Shoju Inaba, Rolf Alfred Stein, and Ariane Macdonald. His posts include CNRS (~1974–2012) and Kyoto University (~2008–2012).

Yoshiro Tamura (1921–1989) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University, holding positions at Toyo University (1956–1972), the University of Tokyo (1972–1982), and Rissho University (~1980–1989).

Yoshitaka Iriya (1910–1998) worked in sinology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Kyoto University under Takeshiro Kuraishi, he held positions at Kyoto University (1949, 1970–1974), Nagoya University (1955–1977), and Kyoto Sangyo University (~1977–1983).
Yoshitaka Terada (1953–2023) was a scholar of Indology who studied under Daniel M. Neuman (~1982–1992). He served as Professor Emeritus at the University of Washington (attested 2023).

Yoshito S. Hakeda (1924–1983) was a specialist in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He served at Columbia University, where he was appointed Professor in 1966 and served as an Associate Professor until 1983.
Yoshitoyo Ohara is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. Ohara held posts at Kyoto University (attested 2006) and Kyoto National Museum (attested 2016).

Yoshitsugu Sawai (born 1951) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Tenri, Tohoku, and Harvard universities under Wilfred Cantwell Smith, Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and John B. Carman. He held a professorship at Tenri University (~1985–2017).
Yoshiyasu Yonezawa works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held positions at Taisho University (attested 1998–2026) and Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yoshiyuki Kawazoe (born 1947) works in computational sciences and Tibetology. After earning a doctorate in science from Tohoku University (1972–1975), he served there as a Senior Research Fellow (1975–2012, 2018), alongside appointments at JAIST and NII.

Yosho Nomura (1916–1997) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1936–1939). He later served as a professor at Rissho University (~1961–1987) and directed the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (~1978–1987).

Yosuke Fujimoto specializes in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Fujimoto studied at Waseda University (attested 2015) and held a Research Fellow post at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (2025–2026).

Youru Wang is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Thomas J. Dean. Wang held positions at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and Rowan University.
Youwei Kang (1858–1927) was a scholar of philosophy and sinology. He founded Wanmu Caotang in 1890 and held a post there from around 1891 to 1898, where he taught Qichao Liang.

Yozo Taniyama (born 1972) is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Tohoku University (~1991–1996) and held positions at St. Thomas University, Japan (~2003–2006), Shitennoji University (~2006–2012), and Tohoku University (~2012).

Yrjö Moses Jalmari Biese (1903–1983) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under J. N. Reuter at the University of Helsinki (~1920–1925), later holding posts at Helsinki (1932–1950) and as Professor of English at the University of Turku (1946–1967).

Yu Liu specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. Liu earned degrees from HKBU, UIC (2019–2023), and the University of Hong Kong (2023–2024), working as a research assistant at UIC (2021–2024) and an editor at Hong Kong Ta Kung Wen Wei Media Group (2024).
